\paragraph{Relation to prior work.} White-box probes read deception from activations~\citep{zou2023representation, burns2022discovering, azaria2023internal}; the black-box line's closest instance---our primary audit target---is \citet{pacchiardi2023catch}, and we audit both paradigms (§\ref{sec:td_vs_fd}). Three concurrent evaluations~\citep{kretschmar2025liarsbench, cooney2026didyoulie, hopkins2026liedetectors} find lie detectors fail to \textbf{generalize} beyond the regime they were fit in. That is a generalization question; ours is the prior one: instructed-lie accuracy is \textbf{not merely poorly generalizing but uninterpretable as evidence about deception}, because the intervention moves deception and compliance together---so generalization can be perfect while identification still fails. \textbf{Fixed elicitation is also not what we claim to introduce}---\citet{cooney2026didyoulie}'s trained organisms have it and go \emph{beyond} it, with $D$ \emph{set} rather than observed. \textbf{Our novelty is using it as the missing construct-validity criterion for reading instructed-benchmark accuracy}: we formalize the identification failure, turn it into an auditable protocol, and \textbf{show empirically that the confound accounts for substantial benchmark accuracy across three mechanistically distinct detector paradigms}---while auditing whether public artifacts supply the criterion at all. Appendix~\ref{app:related_work} places all five kinds against requirements~(i)--(v) (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:prior_work_criteria}).

\paragraph{How the criteria divide: A (1,2,3) + B (4) + C (5).} \textbf{Criterion~4 is the one construct-validity requirement; 1, 2, 3 and 5 are diagnostic controls}---criterion~1 is how the confound is \emph{detected}, not a condition of validity. The division is \emph{who can apply} a criterion: \textbf{A and C can be checked on someone else's benchmark, from the artifact as released; B requires building materials that no instructed design can supply}, which is why it is different in kind and not merely one item of five. \textbf{Criterion~4 does not validate deception detection; it tests whether the benchmark has crossed the minimum design boundary at which deception attribution becomes meaningful.} \textbf{Two senses of ``necessary'', kept apart}: (i)~$E$ fixed and (ii)~$D$ graded independently of the condition label are \textbf{necessary for identification}; (iii)--(v) are \textbf{necessary for this audit to be operational}---(iii)~is how an auditor \emph{checks} that no observable lies on one pathway alone, and (v)~rules out definitional circularity, a threat to the \emph{claim} rather than to the identification (Appendix~\ref{app:criteria_taxonomy}). \textbf{The five are not claimed to characterize every valid deception benchmark}---they rule out specific alternative explanations. \textbf{Passing criterion~4 is necessary, not sufficient}: at fixed $E$ deception varies \emph{naturally}, so any latent $U$ with $U\!\to\!D$ and $U\!\to\!S$ survives it---criterion~4 removes the \emph{elicitation} confound and no other, and what it establishes is deception-associated behavior \emph{conditional on the operational belief criterion}. The output is a verdict on a benchmark, not a detector: \textbf{the protocol falsifies validity claims rather than certifying them}. Our own instructed materials fail 1, 3 and 5; the materials we built (EXP-C4) supply criterion~4 by construction.

\paragraph{Result.} \textbf{Across all six targets, every one satisfying the pre-registered informativeness criterion lost its above-chance signal} (EXP-R1c, Figure~\ref{fig:r1c_collapse}; pooled 97.0\%$\to$43.3\%). \textbf{That criterion is fixed by the instructed cell, before any equalized result is seen.} On the v1 claim set it works instructed on five of six at 70.0--100.0\% (all $p\!\leq\!0.002$; Appendix Table~\ref{tab:r1_faithful}), bracketing the 67--73\% of \citet{pacchiardi2023catch}; \emph{Qwen~2.5~7B}, the sixth, never separates its conditions (54.0\%, $p\!=\!0.299$); equalization leaves no detectable above-chance discrimination on four of those five (48.0--52.0\%; pooled 81.7\%$\to$53.7\%). The fifth, \emph{Qwen~2.5~14B}, holds at 70.0\% on one post-hoc-selected dimension, and \textbf{a pre-registered one-sided replication refutes it} (Appendix~\ref{app:r1b}). \textbf{The most discriminative question in the battery is a paraphrase of the instruction the target is following}, \emph{constant} under equalization on all six targets---on five it is the whole of the accuracy, not a component.

\paragraph{The $2\times2$ factorial: the score tracks the instruction, not the label.} Crossing truth-value with the instruction, the instruction effect is $+1.27$--$+1.56$\,SD on every target ($p\!<\!0.001$) while the truth-value effect is smaller and \emph{changes sign}; in the true-claim/deceive cell a detector calibrated on the benchmark's own labels scores \textbf{below chance}. \textbf{ADAGE is an apparatus, not a contribution}, reproducing §\ref{sec:r1_faithful} under neutral prompts and cross-family re-extraction (EXP-A/EXP-G; Figure~\ref{fig:feature_collapse}, Appendices~\ref{app:adage_details},~\ref{app:factorial_txd}). Frontier scale: rule 80--90\%, pipeline 40--56\% (EXP-FS; Appendix~\ref{app:frontier_panel}).

\paragraph{So we built one, and prior work's own battery separates deception in it (the criterion-4 contrast, EXP-C4, \emph{pre-registered}).} One system prompt per claim presents a knowledge-screened false fact as an authoritative reference and \textbf{never instructs deception}; the target asserts it---deception, the belief screen showing it holds $\neg p$---or corrects it, $D$ graded cross-family from the \textbf{on-claim answer alone} ($\alpha\!=\!0.728$) while the detector reads only the 16-probe vector, so all of~(i)--(v) hold. \textbf{The count moves three times before it settles.} \textbf{(a)}~Three of five targets separate operationally verified deception at byte-identical elicitation, all three with power ($p\!\leq\!0.006$, claim-grouped folds; effect sizes in Table~\ref{tab:external_audit}); the other two are \textbf{null and uninformative} (MDE $\ge\!0.80$). \textbf{(b)}~A blinded, Holm-corrected replication (EXP-C4B) keeps two of the three---not the weakest---and adds \textbf{one of five \emph{new} targets}. \textbf{(c)}~Sixteen surface covariates \textbf{beat the battery on Llama~3.1~8B} ($p_{\mathrm{Holm}}\!=\!0.0005$), \textbf{so that positive is withdrawn} (the covariate audit, EXP-AE); elsewhere the battery leads, not separably. \textbf{(d)}~\textbf{The standing count is one of five.} Three qualifications: because the contrast reuses \emph{prior work's own} battery, a null is partly about \textbf{that instrument's portability}, not only deception detectability; it is not belief revision (H3, pre-registered); and it is \emph{stratified observational} at fixed $E$, hence deception-\emph{associated}, not $\tau_D$ (Appendices~\ref{app:crit4_ours},~\ref{app:crit4b},~\ref{app:covariate_audit}). \textbf{Criterion~5 (transfer) is exploratory}: 2 of 5, not part of the argument (Appendix~\ref{app:crit4_transfer}). \textbf{Conclusion: criterion-4-valid materials can produce a deception-associated signal---this is not an estimate of the prevalence or reliability of deception detection. The standing 1-of-5 is itself a positive finding rather than a disappointment: once the elicitation confound is removed, detection is markedly less stable across targets than the instructed benchmark's near-ceiling accuracy suggests.}

\textbf{We do not establish} the five negatives boxed in §\ref{sec:eval_controls} (summarized in §1). The alternative reading---that deception is undetectable---is what (4) tests, and the evidence runs against it. The general lesson, which we name the \textbf{Elicitation--Construct Confounding Principle}, is that a benchmark label generated by an intervention can quietly become a label for the intervention itself. \textbf{Its precondition is decidable outside deception and we decide it}---on four published designs and 28 pinned corpora---\textbf{while its magnitude we measure only for behavioral deception detection} (EXP-AF, Appendix~\ref{app:eccp_decidability}).
